_comment: Project-shape profiles — the single source of truth for which workflows
each profile switches off. Read by cli/slopstopper/profiles.py (the CLI)
AND by install.sh (via python3, resolved from the source checkout), so
there is exactly one copy of this mapping in the project.
A profile only ever SUBTRACTS workflows. `workflows.disabled` in
.slopstopper.yml adds to a profile's set; `workflows.enabled` removes
from it, so an adopter can keep an individual check the profile drops.
Adding a profile: add an entry here, then follow the AGENTS.md row for

ui.summary: A web UI — a site or app that serves HTML to a browser.
ui.detail: Every check applies. This is the default when `profile:` is unset, so an existing install keeps behaving exactly as before. The API checks are included and stay inert until you configure `api.health.path` / `api.headers.paths` — a UI repo with API routes should get them without having to discover workflows.enabled.

api.summary: An HTTP API — JSON/gRPC endpoints with no browser-rendered surface.
api.detail: Drops the eight browser-and-SEO checks: they assume HTML, a DOM and a public web surface, so on an API repo they fail rather than no-op. Keeps the two API checks (api-health, api-headers), DAST (ZAP scans an API fine) and CSP exceptions (APIs still set response headers; the check stays inert until you set headers.source).

library.summary: A library, CLI or package — no deployed surface of any kind.
library.detail: Drops everything that needs a URL: the eight browser-and-SEO checks, DAST and CSP exceptions, and the two API checks. What remains is the static-analysis layer, which is the whole of what applies to code that nothing serves.
